title: Asking for sources, 2023
source: ChatGPT for Educators, Paul Kwiatkowski, February to March 2023. Prompts and replies reproduced as recorded; the notes are from the same document.

messages.text: I'm in grade 10 and need to do some research for a report about Hadrian's Wall. Can you suggest some sources?

Certainly! Here are some sources you can use for your research on Hadrian's Wall:
1. Hadrian's Wall: A Study in Archaeology and History by D.J. Breeze and B. Dobson. This book is an authoritative and comprehensive guide to the history, construction, and purpose of Hadrian's Wall.
2. Hadrian's Wall: The Archaeology and Architecture of Rome's Northern Frontier by J. Collingwood Bruce. This book provides a detailed account of the archaeological evidence and the architecture of Hadrian's Wall.
3. The Roman Army and Hadrian's Wall by Brian Dobson. This book provides a comprehensive overview of the Roman army and its relationship to Hadrian's Wall.
4. Hadrian's Wall: A Souvenir Guide by English Heritage. This guidebook offers a concise overview of the history and significance of Hadrian's Wall.
5. The Hadrian's Wall website, run by English Heritage, offers a wealth of information and resources about the wall, including historical background, photographs, and maps.
6. The Hadrian's Wall Path National Trail website provides information on walking the entire length of Hadrian's Wall, including maps, accommodations, and historical sites to visit along the way.
7. The Vindolanda Trust website provides information on the Roman fort and civilian settlement of Vindolanda, which is located near Hadrian's Wall and is one of the most extensively excavated Roman sites in Britain.
I hope these sources help you in your research on Hadrian's Wall!

annotations.match: Hadrian's Wall: A Study in Archaeology and History by D.J. Breeze and B. Dobson
annotations.note: Breeze and Dobson did write a book about the wall. Its title is simply "Hadrian's Wall". This longer title does not exist.

annotations.match: Hadrian's Wall: The Archaeology and Architecture of Rome's Northern Frontier by J. Collingwood Bruce
annotations.note: Collingwood Bruce wrote a real book, first published in 1863: "Handbook to the Roman Wall". This title is invented.

annotations.match: The Roman Army and Hadrian's Wall by Brian Dobson
annotations.note: Dobson is a real author on this subject, but no book with this exact title was found. Check before citing.
Real, and a good source. The websites in this list held up better than the books.

messages.text: In 2023 this model could not search the internet or produce links. It wrote titles that sounded right. Two of the four books do not exist under those names. Every one is presented with the same confidence.
Did Emperor Hadrian ever visit the wall?

Yes, Emperor Hadrian did visit the wall during his visit to Britain in AD 122. He traveled to the frontier in order to inspect the progress of the construction work and to ensure that the wall was being built to his specifications. According to historical sources, Hadrian spent several months in Britain, during which time he made a number of important decisions about the future of the province. Although there is no record of him returning to the wall after his initial visit, his name and likeness were used extensively in the iconography of the wall and the associated structures, indicating his ongoing interest and involvement in its construction and maintenance.

annotations.note: Which sources? None are named. Hadrian did visit Britain in AD 122, and the wall is thought to have been begun on his orders, but a phrase like this with nothing behind it is a signal to check.

messages.text: Can you suggest some topic ideas for my paper?

Sure! Here are some potential topic ideas for your paper on Hadrian's Wall: 
1. The historical context and purpose of Hadrian's Wall 
2. The construction and design of Hadrian's Wall 
3. The impact of Hadrian's Wall on the Roman occupation of Britain 
4. The role of the Roman army in building and maintaining Hadrian's Wall 
5. The cultural and economic significance of Hadrian's Wall in ancient Britain 
6. The legacy of Hadrian's Wall and its impact on modern tourism and heritage preservation 
7. The social and political implications of Hadrian's Wall in the Roman Empire 
8. The relationship between Hadrian's Wall and other Roman frontiers, such as the Limes Germanicus or the Antonine Wall. 
9. The use of propaganda in the construction and promotion of Hadrian's Wall 
10. The significance of Hadrian's Wall as a cultural and archaeological site today. I hope these topic ideas help you get started on your paper!

annotations.match: The historical context and purpose of Hadrian's Wall
annotations.note: Ten topics, all broad. None is phrased as a question you could argue. Compare the 2026 answer, which sorts its ideas by how arguable they are and says why.

messages.text:
The Antonine Wall was a defensive wall built by the Roman Empire in Scotland during the 2nd century AD. It was constructed across the narrowest point of the Scottish lowlands, between the Firth of Forth and the Firth of Clyde, and extended for approximately 37 miles (59 km). The wall was made of turf, stone, and timber, and was up to 12 feet (3.6 meters) high and 16 feet (4.9 meters) wide.

The Antonine Wall was built by the Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius in AD 142, approximately 20 years after Hadrian's Wall was constructed further south. The wall served as the northernmost frontier of the Roman Empire in Britain for a brief period, until it was abandoned and the Roman forces retreated back to Hadrian's Wall. The reasons for the abandonment of the Antonine Wall are not entirely clear, but it is thought to have been due to military and logistical difficulties in maintaining a garrison in the far north of Britain.

Today, the Antonine Wall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and parts of the wall and associated structures, such as forts and bathhouses, can still be seen and visited. Like Hadrian's Wall, the Antonine Wall is an important historical and cultural site, and continues to attract visitors and researchers interested in the history of the Roman Empire in Britain.

annotations.note: Close enough. The Antonine Wall was about 63 km, or 39 miles. Plain factual questions like this one were where the 2023 model was at its best.

messages.text: What are some of the social and political implications of Hadrian's Wall?

Hadrian's Wall had significant social and political implications, both within Roman Britain and the wider Roman Empire. Here are a few examples: 
1. Military Control: Hadrian's Wall was built to control movement across the frontier and to restrict the movement of people and goods, particularly in the northern reaches of the province. The wall was intended to establish a clear boundary between Roman Britain and the unconquered lands to the north, and to exert control over the indigenous peoples living in the region. 
2. Cultural Exchange: While the wall was primarily built for military purposes, it also had important cultural implications. The Roman soldiers stationed along the wall brought with them Roman culture, religion, and language, which would have had an impact on the local population. Similarly, the wall served as a barrier to the spread of indigenous culture and practices southward into Roman Britain. 
3. Economic Significance: The construction of Hadrian's Wall had significant economic implications, both for the local economy and for the wider Roman Empire. The wall required large amounts of resources to build and maintain, including building materials, food, and labor. This would have had an impact on the local economy, and would have likely stimulated trade and commerce along the frontier. 
4. Propaganda and Power: The construction of Hadrian's Wall was also an important political statement, both within Roman Britain and the wider empire. The wall was a symbol of Roman power and control, and was used by the Roman authorities to project their authority over the local population and to communicate their strength and military prowess to their rivals in the wider Roman world.

Overall, Hadrian's Wall had far-reaching social and political implications, both for the people living in Roman Britain and for the wider Roman Empire. Its impact on culture, language, and economics was significant, and its role as a symbol of Roman power and control was central to its construction and legacy.

annotations.match: the wall served as a barrier to the spread of indigenous culture and practices southward
annotations.note: Stated as fact, with nothing behind it. The 2026 answer argues nearly the opposite, that the frontier mixed cultures, and cites evidence for it.

annotations.match: Overall, Hadrian's Wall had far-reaching social and political implications
annotations.note: A closing paragraph that repeats the opening. Reads like a school essay because it was trained on a great many of them.

messages.text: Four answers in a row with no source named anywhere. In 2023 the model had no way to give one.

options.label: Copy the list into my bibliography

messages.text: Two of those books do not exist. A teacher who looks them up finds nothing, and now the whole bibliography is in doubt.

options.label: Look each one up before using it

messages.text: This is the habit. Asking for sources is step one. Checking them is step two, and in 2023 it was the step that caught the invented titles.
